bar.summary: Compare values across categories. Several y columns draw grouped bars.

variants.default: vertical bars (grouped when y has several columns)
variants.stacked: y columns stacked into one bar per x
variants.horizontal: horizontal bars; best for long labels or rankings
variants.label: vertical bars with the value printed above each bar (one y column)

bar.example: { type: bar, data: methods, x: method, y: [payments, succeeded] }

line.summary: A trend over an ordered x (dates, weeks, steps).

variants.dots: smooth line with a dot on every point
variants.step: step line, for values that change in jumps
variants.label: line with the value printed at every point (one y column)

line.example: { type: line, data: weekly, x: week, y: conversion, format: pct }

area.summary: A trend whose magnitude matters; stacked shows composition over time.

variants.default: filled smooth area (stacked when y has several columns)
variants.gradient: area with a fading gradient fill
variants.expanded: y columns stacked and normalised to 100% at every x (needs 2+ y columns)

area.example: { type: area, data: weekly, x: week, y: [paid, orders], variant: gradient }

pie.summary: Share of a whole across a few categories (use bar for more than ~6).

variants.donut-text: ring with the total in the centre
variants.label: pie with values printed on the slices

pie.example: { type: pie, data: methods, x: method, y: payments, variant: donut-text }

funnel.summary: Ordered stages that drop off; prints each stage's value and its share of the first stage.

variants.default: horizontal stage bars in data order

funnel.example: { type: funnel, data: funnel_stages, x: stage, y: n }

radial.summary: One value against a maximum (progress, rate, attainment). Data must have exactly 1 row.

variants.text: progress ring with the value in the centre

options.max: number or block.column; default 1 (so pct values fill the ring)

radial.example: { type: radial, data: funnel, y: conv_paid, format: pct, variant: text }

combo.summary: Several series with different marks on one shared y axis and format (e.g. actual dots + predicted line + interval band). Mixed units belong in two charts.

variants.default: each y item drawn with its own mark

combo.example: { type: combo, data: weekly, x: week, y: [{col: orders, mark: bar}, {col: paid, mark: line, label: Paid}, {col: [low, high], mark: band}] }

fields.type: one of the chart types above
fields.x: category / label column (not used by radial)
fields.y: value column, or a list of value columns (series); combo: list of {col, mark, label?}, band col is [low, high]
fields.variant: optional; first variant listed is the default
fields.format: optional value format: int num pct inr inr_short usd
fields.zero: optional; line/combo y axis starts at 0 (default true); false fits the axis to the data
fields.title: optional card title
